source: spec-mutation day 1, surviving mutant M08 (codepoint-key-sort). draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §3.1 step 2 imports RFC 8785 whole; RFC 8785 §3.2.3 sorts member names on their UTF-16 code units. Formalization status, corrected 2026-08-04: the §3.2.3 sort key IS now formalized — the Jcss Lean development defines it as `utf16Units`, derives the key uniqueness of §3.2.3 from strictness of the order alone (`keysSorted_keys_nodup`, by irreflexivity; injectivity is not used), and separately proves the sort key injective (`utf16Units_inj`), so the sort key determines the key string and the induced key order is antisymmetric — the canonicity half. What is still outside the proved fragment is the ordering clause itself: `KeysSorted` is not a hypothesis of any serialization theorem, nothing proves that a canonicalizer PRODUCES that order, and no Lean theorem pins the byte strings below — so killing M08 still rests on this vector. Field `formalization_status` records the detail, the audited axiom closures, and the superseded version-1 sentence. See DAY2-REPORT.md §3 (vault-side day-2 report) for the mutation pass that produced this vector.

formalization_status.development: papers/jcss-canonicalization-lean/deposit/jcss in the Tyche research vault (Lean 4.32.2). `lake build` runs the `#print axioms` audit in Jcss/Axioms.lean; the run of 2026-08-04 completed successfully and printed 39 audit lines.
formalization_status.now_formalized: `KeysSorted` was redefined on 2026-08-04 from Lean's String `<` (code-point lexicographic) to strict ascending order on `utf16Units : String → List Nat`, the UTF-16 code-unit sequence of RFC 8785 §3.2.3 — so the development now sorts on the key this vector is about. Injectivity of that key is a kernel-checked theorem, `utf16Units_inj`, proved from prefix-freedom of the encoding (`utf16CharUnits_prefix`, then the list induction `utf16Chars_inj`); prefix-freedom holds because Lean's `Char` is a Unicode scalar value, so the surrogate block U+D800-U+DFFF is excluded by construction. Independently — not as a corollary of injectivity — `keysSorted_keys_nodup`: a `KeysSorted` object has pairwise distinct keys, proved from strictness of the order alone (irreflexivity of `<`; the proof never touches `utf16Units_inj`). What injectivity buys instead is antisymmetry of the induced key order — with totality of the lexicographic order, the sorted member list of an object is unique — and that the §3.2.3 sort key determines the key string.

audited_axiom_closures.criterion: Every closure is a subset of {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} — no `sorryAx`, no project-local axiom. Read off the `lake build` output of 2026-08-04, not transcribed from an earlier note.

formalization_status.still_not_formalized: The ordering clause is not a hypothesis of any serialization result: `ser_inj` and the fork theorems (`exclusion_depth_fork`, `member_removal_fork` and their `jcs-n` counterparts) do not assume `KeysSorted`, and nothing in the development proves that a canonicalizer PRODUCES UTF-16 code-unit order. Across the whole development `KeysSorted` is consumed as a hypothesis by exactly one theorem, `keysSorted_keys_nodup`, which draws key uniqueness out of it. The byte strings and digests under `cases` below are not pinned by any Lean theorem either: deposit/verify/PrintPins.lean prints the exclusion-depth and member-removal payloads only, and the development's sole non-BMP witness is the sanity check `#guard utf16Units "\u{1F600}" == [0xD83D, 0xDE00]`. Mutant M08 is therefore killed by this vector, not by the proof development.
formalization_status.superseded_v1_text: Version 1 of this vector (2026-08-03) asserted in `source`: 'NOT machine-checked: the Jcss Lean development models key order as `KeysSorted` (Lean String `<`, i.e. code points) and no theorem uses that predicate, so the ordering clause is outside the formalized fragment.' Both halves were falsified by the Lean change of 2026-08-04. The sentence is kept here so that the correction is auditable rather than silent.
formalization_status.regeneration_note: Updated 2026-08-04: the day-2 harness day2_vectors.py was brought up to date the same day as this correction and now itself emits the corrected version-2 `source` text (with `version: 2` and `corrected: 2026-08-04`), so re-running it no longer reverts the correction. The harness does not regenerate `formalization_status`: it carries this object forward verbatim from the existing on-disk kat-utf16-key-order.json and refuses to write any vectors at all if that file is missing or lacks the field — so a re-run cannot silently drop this record, but it also cannot update it, and later changes to the Lean development must still be recorded here by hand (or the harness updated first). The harness's original abort gate is unchanged: if its two independent digest computations disagree on any byte string or digest, it aborts and writes no vectors.

copies.provenance_note: Exact per-file hashes are pinned by the deposit MANIFEST.sha256 and by git, not restated inside this vector, so this record stays valid across pushes and does not need editing when a copy is pushed.

rule: Member names MUST be sorted by UTF-16 code unit, not by Unicode code point (RFC 8785 §3.2.3, imported by §3.1 step 2). The two orders coincide on every member name inside the Basic Multilingual Plane and diverge only above U+FFFF, because a non-BMP name begins with a high surrogate in D800-DBFF, which is numerically below any BMP name in E000-FFFF while its code point is above. An implementation that produces a must_fail digest below sorts on code points and MUST FAIL this KAT. A vector corpus containing no member name above U+FFFF cannot distinguish the two policies at all.
why_no_corpus_vector_catches_this: Every member name in vectors/ at 7c9f6421 is BMP (verified by per-character scan on day 1), and on BMP-only inputs the two sort orders are extensionally equal, so no BMP-only corpus can ever kill this mutant.

rfc8785_primary_source.requirement_quote: Property name strings to be sorted are formatted as arrays of UTF-16 [UNICODE] code units.  The sorting is based on pure value comparisons, where code units are treated as unsigned integers, independent of locale settings.
rfc8785_primary_source.rfc_note_on_this_exact_divergence: Note: For the purpose of obtaining a deterministic property order, sorting of data encoded in UTF-8 or UTF-32 would also work, but the outcome for JSON data like above would differ and thus be incompatible with this specification.  However, in practice, property names are rarely defined outside of 7-bit ASCII, making it possible to sort string data in UTF-8 or UTF-32 format without conversion to UTF-16 and still be compatible with JCS.
rfc8785_primary_source.note: A code-point sort is exactly the UTF-32 sort the RFC names as incompatible, and the RFC's own second sentence is the reason a corpus never notices: names outside 7-bit ASCII are rare. The case 'rfc8785-sorting-example' below is the RFC's test data verbatim, and its must_pass byte string reproduces the RFC's stated expected argument order.
rfc_expected_argument_order: Latin Small Letter O With Diaeresis

cases.note: Two members only. U+1F600 GRINNING FACE (UTF-16 D83D DE00) and U+FB33 HEBREW LETTER DALET WITH DAGESH (UTF-16 FB33). UTF-16 order puts the emoji first (D83D < FB33); code-point order puts it last (0x1F600 > 0xFB33).

must_pass.note: One digest serves both algorithms: no member of the witness is null, an empty array, or an empty object, so jcs-n normalization is the identity here and the jcs-s digest is the same value (2aa3f5086e32bb90ce39c508a6f40fd72e792684f130d0f3b896ea191368f1e3).

must_fail.note: Identical to the jcs-n wrong branch on this witness, for the same reason the must_pass digest is algorithm-independent: normalization is the identity. Named separately so that neither digest is left unscoped.

cases.note: The seven-member sorting example of RFC 8785 §3.2.3, verbatim. Under the conforming order the emoji sorts between U+20AC and U+FB33; under a code-point sort it moves to the end. Included because it is the RFC's own witness, so a reader need not take our pair on trust.

digests_computed_by: Recomputed 2026-08-03 by two implementations that agreed on every byte string and every digest: (1) a standard-library-only Python RFC 8785 serializer written for this run, whose UTF-16 sort key is built by explicit surrogate-pair decomposition rather than by str.encode('utf-16-be'); (2) the CPB reference implementation cpb.canonicalize at 7c9f6421 -- for the conforming branch as published, and for the code-point branch with the day-1 M08 patch applied, which is the only way the reference emits that order. Harness: day2/day2_vectors.py.
